steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Stakeholders: any person or group with an interest in a business. Internal: owners, employees, managers. External: customers, suppliers, local community, government, pressure groups.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Stakeholder objectives often conflict: owners want maximum profit (low wages, high prices); employees want higher wages and better conditions; customers want low prices and high quality; local community wants jobs but less pollution; government wants tax revenue and compliance.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Managing stakeholder conflict: compromise, negotiation, prioritisation. Businesses cannot satisfy all stakeholders equally - they must balance competing interests based on power and importance.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Stakeholder influence varies: owners/shareholders have high influence (can appoint directors); employees can take industrial action; customers can take their business elsewhere; pressure groups can damage reputation through social media campaigns.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Identify four stakeholders of a large supermarket and explain what each would want from the business. | Explain how a conflict might arise between employees and owners of a business, and how it could be resolved. | A factory wants to expand, creating 200 jobs but increasing traffic and noise. Evaluate the competing stakeholder interests.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Owners: maximum profit and return on investment. Employees: fair wages, job security, safe working conditions. Customers: low prices, wide product range, convenient location. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always identify stakeholders as internal or external For each stakeholder, state WHAT they want and WHY Show both sides of any conflict before suggesting a resolution
